cards: Nader Shah was a military commander from the Turkic Afshar tribe of Khorasan who founded the Afsharid Empire and reigned as Shah of Iran from 1736 to 1747.
Peter the Great was Tsar and first Emperor of Russia, proclaimed emperor in 1721 after victory over Sweden in the Great Northern War.
Maria Theresa was the only female ruler of the Habsburg lands, inheriting them in 1740 under the Pragmatic Sanction.
Catherine the Great, or Catherine II, was empress of Russia from 1762 to 1796.
Taksin was a Siamese general of Chinese descent who rallied resistance after the Burmese destroyed Ayutthaya in 1767 and was crowned king at Thonburi.
Karim Khan Zand was the founder of the Zand dynasty, who ruled most of Iran from Shiraz after the collapse of Afsharid power, and died in 1779.
Frederick the Great, Frederick II of Prussia, was king from 1740.
Charles III of Spain, previously king of Naples and Sicily, ruled Spain from 1759 to 1788.
Charles XII was king of Sweden from 1697 to 1718 and a commander of great tactical skill.
George III was king of Great Britain and Elector, later King, of Hanover from 1760, and king of the United Kingdom from its creation in 1801.
Túpac Amaru II, born José Gabriel Condorcanqui, was a kuraka of the Cusco region who claimed descent from the last Inca ruler, Túpac Amaru.
Baji Rao I was the Peshwa, or chief minister, of the Maratha state from 1720 to 1740.
Voltaire, the pen name of François-Marie Arouet, was a French writer and philosopher and the most famous figure of the Enlightenment.
James Cook was a British naval officer who led three voyages of exploration in the Pacific between 1768 and 1779.
Horatio Nelson was a British admiral, the most celebrated naval commander of the Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars.
Hyder Ali was a soldier who rose to command the army of the Kingdom of Mysore and from 1761 ruled it in place of the Wodeyar kings.
Alaungpaya was the founder of the Konbaung dynasty of Burma, reigning from 1752 to 1760.
Jean-Jacques Rousseau was a Genevan-born philosopher, writer and composer whose works shaped the political thought of the Enlightenment and the French Revolution.
Tipu Sultan was ruler of Mysore from 1782, succeeding his father Hyder Ali.
Karl Theodor von Dalberg was the last Elector and Archbishop of Mainz and Archchancellor of the Holy Roman Empire.
Victor Amadeus II was duke of Savoy from 1675.
Prithvi Narayan Shah was king of Gorkha from 1743 and the founder of modern Nepal.
Benjamin Franklin was a Philadelphia printer, writer, scientist and statesman.
Chhatrasal was a Bundela Rajput leader who fought the Mughal Empire and founded an independent kingdom in Bundelkhand, with its capital at Panna.
Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher (1742–1819) was a Prussian field marshal of the Napoleonic Wars.
Montesquieu, Charles-Louis de Secondat, Baron de La Brède et de Montesquieu, was a French magistrate and political philosopher of the Enlightenment.
William Pitt the Younger was Prime Minister of Great Britain from 1783 to 1801 and again from 1804 to 1806, taking office at the age of 24.
Bodawpaya was the sixth king of the Konbaung dynasty of Burma, reigning from 1782 to 1819.
Francis I (1708–1765), born Francis Stephen, was Duke of Lorraine from 1729 until 1737, when he gave up the duchy under the settlement of the War of the Polish Succession and received the Grand…
Johann Sebastian Bach was a German composer and organist, born at Eisenach.
Kamehameha I was a chief of Hawaiʻi Island who conquered Maui, Molokaʻi and Oʻahu in a series of campaigns, winning the decisive Battle of Nuʻuanu in 1795.
Cesare Beccaria (1738–1794) was an Italian jurist, philosopher and economist of the Milanese Enlightenment.
Charles VI was Holy Roman Emperor from 1711 to 1740 and the last male Habsburg of the senior line.
Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies
Ferdinand I of the Two Sicilies was a Bourbon king who ruled Naples as Ferdinand IV from 1759.
Frederick I was the last duke and first king of Württemberg.
George Frideric Handel was a German-born composer who spent most of his career in London.
George Washington was a Virginia planter and soldier who commanded the Continental Army in the American Revolutionary War and forced the British surrender at Yorktown in 1781.
Herman Willem Daendels was a Dutch Patriot and general who served as governor-general of the Dutch East Indies from 1808 to 1811 for Louis Bonaparte's Kingdom of Holland.
Joachim Murat was a French cavalry commander and Marshal of the Empire who married Napoleon's sister Caroline.
José Fernando de Abascal was a Spanish officer who served as viceroy of Peru from 1806 to 1816.
